Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Which statement is correct?

options.A: Normative economics concerns the description of economic models.
options.B: Normative economics is objective and factual.
options.C: Positive economics can be tested by data and evidence.
options.D: Positive economics is subjective and offers a value judgement.

questions.questionText: Consumers do not use enough of a product to maximise their private benefit because they have imperfect information about the product. How would an economist classify this product?

options.A: demerit good
options.B: free good
options.C: merit good
options.D: public good

questions.questionText: What is meant by the division of labour?

options.A: Each worker specialises in a different task in production.
options.B: Some workers work part-time and others work full-time.
options.C: The same amount of output per hour is produced by each worker.
options.D: Workers divide their time between different jobs.

questions.questionText: What describes a market supply curve?

options.A: It is downward sloping.
options.B: It is the same as the aggregate supply curve.
options.C: It is the sum of all firms’ supply curves for a product.
options.D: It is the supply of all products within an economy.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, D is the demand curve for Indian tea exports and S is the supply curve when there is a tax on tea exports. S price S x z w y D O quantity The Indian government removes the tax, which causes the supply curve to shift to S . Which areas in the diagram measure the resulting loss in tax revenue to the Indian government and the resulting gain in consumer surplus? loss in tax gain in revenue consumer surplus

options.A: x w + y
options.B: x x + z
options.C: x + y z
options.D: x + y x + z

options.A: B D S S price price D E p p E O q O q quantity quantity
options.C: D S D price price S E p E p D O q O q quantity quantity

questions.questionText: In the diagram, the supply curve shows the number of spaces in a car park and the demand curves show the demand for spaces on four different days (D , D , D and D ).
An indirect tax is imposed on a product in a competitive market. Under which circumstances would the value of the consumer surplus be most likely to remain unchanged?

options.A: New substitutes are developed for the product and production costs rise.
options.B: Some producers merge so there is less competition in the market.
options.C: The product is an inferior good, consumer incomes increase and production costs rise.
options.D: The product is a normal good, consumer incomes increase and production costs fall.

questions.questionText: How might a firm raise the value of the price elasticity of supply for its product?

options.A: decrease the amount of labour that it employs
options.B: employ new technology to increase its productive capacity
options.C: increase advertising expenditure to generate more revenue
options.D: reduce the level of stocks in order to cut costs

questions.questionText: Shoe manufacturers often use leather to make their most expensive shoes. Due to a world shortage of leather, the price of leather has risen. What will be the effect of this price change?

options.A: The demand curve for leather shoes will shift to the left.
options.B: The demand curve for a substitute for leather shoes will shift to the right.
options.C: The supply curve for leather shoes will shift to the right.
options.D: The supply curve for a substitute for leather to make expensive shoes will shift to the right.

questions.questionText: The diagram represents the market for a good. P price S X Y D Z 1 O quantity Which statement is correct?

options.A: OX represents the price above which no producer wishes to stay in the market.
options.B: OZ represents the minimum price consumers are prepared to pay.
options.C: PYZ represents the total consumer surplus.
options.D: XYZ represents the total producer surplus.

questions.questionText: The economics department of a university calculates that the price elasticity of demand for the products of a local firm is between –1.1 and –1.3. Which decision could be justified by the research?

options.A: Increase prices to increase profit.
options.B: Invest in more capital to increase output.
options.C: Reduce advertising to reduce costs.
options.D: Reduce prices to increase revenue.

questions.questionText: A specific tax is imposed on a product for which the elasticity of supply is zero. Which statement is correct?

options.A: The burden of this tax will fall entirely on consumers.
options.B: The burden of this tax will fall entirely on suppliers.
options.C: The burden of this tax will fall mainly on consumers.
options.D: The burden of this tax will fall mainly on suppliers.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a market where a government has set a minimum price of OM. S price M minimum price P D O quantity What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: At prices above OM, there would be a surplus of the good.
options.B: At the minimum price OM, there would be a shortage of the good.
options.C: Price will fall automatically from OM to OP.
options.D: The minimum price will be ineffective.

questions.questionText: What would supporters of a nationalised public transport service expect to be the most likely outcome from the privatisation of train and bus services?

options.A: fewer destinations served by trains and buses
options.B: lower fares
options.C: more frequent services to all destinations
options.D: more people employed in public transport services

questions.questionText: A teenager received a cheque for $50 as a birthday gift from her parents. The teenager paid the cheque into her savings account at the bank. Why is this gift a transfer payment?

options.A: It did not involve a cash payment.
options.B: It transfers money between bank accounts.
options.C: The parents did not spend their money.
options.D: The teenager did not produce any output.

questions.questionText: What is a necessary characteristic of a public good?

options.A: It has a fixed maximum price.
options.B: It has an opportunity cost of production of zero.
options.C: It is non-excludable.
options.D: It is an essential good.

questions.questionText: What is least likely to change an advanced industrialised economy’s terms of trade?

options.A: its level of labour productivity
options.B: its rate of inflation
options.C: the maintenance of a stable foreign exchange rate
options.D: the occurrence of random supply shocks

Which combination of changes is most likely to lead to an increase in the aggregate price level and the level of real output? income tax rate net exports

options.A: fall decrease
options.B: fall increase
options.C: rise decrease
options.D: rise increase

questions.questionText: Country W conducts 50% of its trade with country X, 30% of its trade with country Y and 20% of its trade with country Z. The initial value of the trade-weighted exchange rate of country W is 100. Country W’s currency appreciates 10% against the currency of country X, depreciates 10% against the currency of country Y and is unchanged against the currency of country Z. What will be the new trade-weighted exchange rate?

The table shows the goods balance and services balance for a country in selected years. goods balance services balance year ($ billion) ($ billion) 2015 +120 –30 2016 +110 –30 2017 +50 –10 2018 +130 –60 2019 +140 –50 Between which years did the overall goods and services balance change the most?
What is not an example of protectionism?

options.A: export subsidies
options.B: import subsidies
options.C: quotas
options.D: tariffs

questions.questionText: What is an expenditure-switching policy to reduce a country’s balance of payments deficit?

options.A: an increase in budget surplus
options.B: an increase in direct taxes
options.C: an increase in import tariffs
options.D: an increase in interest rates

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) for an economy. AS general price AS level 1 AD O real output Which changes in subsidies and indirect taxes would have caused the change in AS shown?

options.A: higher subsidies and higher indirect taxes
options.B: higher subsidies and lower indirect taxes
options.C: lower subsidies and higher indirect taxes
options.D: lower subsidies and lower indirect taxes

questions.questionText: In its recent budget a government increased defence expenditure and also the amount spent on training that increased the productivity of the workforce. The initial equilibrium point is shown by X on the aggregate demand (AD) and aggregate supply (AS) diagram. What would be the equilibrium point after these changes? AS AS general B price level AS X A C D AD AD AD

An increase or decrease in exchange rates can take place in both a floating and a fixed exchange rate system but different terminology is used for each system. What is the correct terminology? decrease in floating increase in fixed

options.A: depreciation appreciation
options.B: depreciation revaluation
options.C: devaluation appreciation
options.D: devaluation revaluation

questions.questionText: In 2018 the United States (US) government reduced direct taxes on consumers and businesses. What are likely to be the effects of these changes on consumption, investment and national output? consumption investment national output

options.A: decrease decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase increase
options.C: increase decrease decrease
options.D: increase increase increase

questions.questionText: A country experienced a significant fall in unemployment but its inflation rate remained low. What could explain this?

options.A: Global competition prevented firms passing on higher costs.
options.B: Increased spending on imports had lowered the exchange rate.
options.C: There was a low level of spare capacity in the economy.
